scenario.name: GitHub Security Lab, CISA & MITRE — GitHub Actions pull_request_target Workflow & Cloud OIDC Token Audit
scenario.overview: Picture an active industrial factory floor with a moving assembly conveyor belt, an articulated yellow robotic arm, steel parts bins, and a final quality-seal stamping desk. During the quiet night shift on the factory floor, a saboteur steps beside the moving assembly conveyor right before the automated quality stamp. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the factory quality stamp station disguised as a regular visitor, then smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches. Only when a quality engineer checks the finished product’s weight and internal wiring against the locked master blueprint cabinet does the factory-line swap appear. In this scenario (T1195.002, GitHub Security Lab, CISA & MITRE, GitHub Actions pull_request_target Workflow & Cloud OIDC Token Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: privileged pull_request_target Trigger, then runner Environment Variable Inspection, then aWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Privileged pull_request_target Trigger, then Runner Environment Variable Inspection, then AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1195.002 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Never combine pull_request_target with actions/checkout of untrusted PR head refs (github.event.pull_request.head.sha); use unprivileged pull_request workflows for building and testing external PRs.

stages.title: Stage 1: Privileged pull_request_target Trigger Checking Out Untrusted Fork PR Head Ref
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1195.002 - Compromise Software Supply Chain)
stages.description: During the quiet night shift on the factory floor, a saboteur steps beside the moving assembly conveyor right before the automated quality stamp. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder approaches the factory quality stamp station disguised as a regular visitor while everyday visitors and the factory quality inspector go about their routine. Unlike pull_request, a workflow triggered by pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository with write permissions and access to secrets/OIDC. When the workflow executes actions/checkout with ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}, untrusted build scripts from the fork execute inside the privileged runner (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with WorkflowTrigger=pull_request_target , Base Repo Context + Write Token, DangerousPattern=actions/checkout ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha, Repository=corp-org/cloud-infra so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes gh api /orgs/corp-org/audit-log?phrase=action:workflows (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , gh api /orgs/corp-org/audit-log?phrase=action:workflows via System / Runtime Execution Inter so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1195.002 during "Privileged pull_request_target Trigger Checking Out Untrusted Fork PR Head Ref" , Unlike pull_request, a workflow triggered by pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository with write permissions and access to secrets/OIDC while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact grep -rn "pull_request_target" .github/workflows/ runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , grep -rn "pull_request_target" .github/workflows/ via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1195.002 during "Privileged pull_request_target Trigger Checking Out Untrusted Fork PR Head Ref" , Unlike pull_request, a workflow triggered by pull_request_target runs in the context of the base repository with write permissions and access to secrets/OIDC while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Runner Environment Variable Inspection & OIDC JWT Token Request
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.001 - Credentials In Files / Environment)
stages.description: The robotic arm pauses for a heartbeat as the saboteur swaps one genuine component on the belt for an identical-looking counterfeit part carrying a hidden wire. Here in Step 2 inside the factory floor, the intruder approaches the factory quality stamp station disguised as a regular visitor without disturbing the original master blueprint cabinet. Executing during the build step, the modified build script reads ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN from the runner process environment to request a signed GitHub OIDC JWT for audience sts.amazonaws.com (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with OidcEndpoint=ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL , &audience=sts.amazonaws.com, TokenSubjectClaim=repo:corp-org/cloud-infra:pull_request, RunnerProcess=/usr/bin/curl spawned by npm test so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ausearch -k github_runner_exec -m SYSCALL -sv yes (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -k github_runner_exec -m SYSCALL -sv yes via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.001 during "Runner Environment Variable Inspection & OIDC JWT Token Request" , Executing during the build step, the modified build script reads ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN from the runner process environment to request a signed GitHub OIDC JWT for audience sts while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact jq '. | select(.permissions."id-token"=="write")' .github/workflows/*.yml runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.permissions."id-token"=="write"' .github/workflows/*.yml via System / Runti so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.001 during "Runner Environment Variable Inspection & OIDC JWT Token Request" , Executing during the build step, the modified build script reads ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN from the runner process environment to request a signed GitHub OIDC JWT for audience sts while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ curl -H "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL&audience=sts.amazonaws.com" / ⇠#2 ACK 59) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 GitHub Actions pull_request_target Runner), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity).

keySpecs.value: Set default workflow permissions to read-only (permissions: contents: read) and grant id-token: write only at the specific deployment job level protected by GitHub Deployment Environments with required reviewers.

stages.title: Stage 3: AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity & CloudTrail Subject Claim Audit
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1550.001 - Application Access Token)
stages.description: The assembly line rolls forward, the factory press stamps the official warranty seal right onto the tampered unit, and trucks ship it to every trusting customer. In this final step inside the factory floor, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches until the assembly line inspection camera catches the mismatch. Because the AWS IAM Role trust policy verified only token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub Like repo:corp-org/cloud-infra:* without restricting the ref to refs/heads/main, sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity succeeds and issues production AWS credentials, logged in CloudTrail (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with CloudTrailEvent=AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, OidcIdentityProvider=token.actions.githubusercontent.com, SubjectClaimLogged=repo:corp-org/cloud-infra:pull_request so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '.Records[] | select(.eventName=="AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity")' cloudtrail.json (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '.Records[] | select.eventName=="AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"' cloudtrail.json via System so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1550.001 during "AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity & CloudTrail Subject Claim Audit" , Because the AWS IAM Role trust policy verified only token while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact aws iam get-role --role-name github-actions-prod-deploy-role runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , aws iam get-role --role-name github-actions-prod-deploy-role against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Clou so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1550.001 during "AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity & CloudTrail Subject Claim Audit" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity (sub=repo:corp-org/cloud-infra:ref:refs/heads/main) / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 GitHub Actions pull_request_target Runner) to Node ④ (#4 ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL (OIDC)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity).

keySpecs.value: Scope AWS IAM OIDC trust policies using strict StringEquals conditions on token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub (e.g., repo:corp-org/cloud-infra:ref:refs/heads/main or environment:production) rather than wildcard repo:* patterns.
